# revit-mcp-tool-generator

🇬🇧 English · **[🇮🇹 Italiano](README.it.md)**

> Build **MCP tools for Revit** by talking to Claude in plain language. No code, no Revit API knowledge needed — describe what you want, Claude builds it, tests it, installs it.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Status: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimental-orange.svg)](#-project-status)
[![Tested on: Revit 2024](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20on-Revit%202024-0696D7.svg)](#-project-status)
[![Tests: 79](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-79%20passing-brightgreen.svg)](#)

---

## ⚠️ Project Status

This is an **experimental project** in early stages (v0.1.0). We built it at [Studioliquid](https://github.com/studioliquid-lab) to solve an internal workflow need at our studio, and decided to open source it to gather feedback from the Revit community.

**What that means in practice**:

- ✅ The 49 backend unit tests pass
- ✅ The end-to-end flow has been verified **only on Revit 2024** with pyRevit Master
- ⚠️ **NOT tested on other Revit versions** (2022/2023/2025+). It might work, but no guarantees
- ⚠️ Bugs and edge cases are expected: not battle-tested
- ⚠️ Internal APIs and patterns may change in upcoming releases (`semver < 1.0`)
- ⚠️ **Use on test projects first**, not production models

### Tested versions

| Component | Version tested |
|---|---|
| Revit | **2024** (build 2024.2) |
| pyRevit | **Master** (4.8.16+) |
| Python (host of the MCP server) | **3.11** / **3.14** |
| Operating system | Windows 11 |

If you try it on other versions, [open an Issue](https://github.com/studioliquid-lab/revit-mcp-tool-generator/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) and let us know how it went — good or bad experience is valuable to expand the compatibility matrix.

We're actively looking for feedback on:
- Bugs, crashes, Revit instability
- Tools that the skill can't generate (or generates incorrectly)
- Suggestions to improve the [cookbook](revit-mcp-tool-generator/references/cookbook.md) and templates
- Workflows and use cases you'd like to see supported

Open an [Issue](https://github.com/studioliquid-lab/revit-mcp-tool-generator/issues) or join the [Discussions](https://github.com/studioliquid-lab/revit-mcp-tool-generator/discussions).

---

## What it does

In Claude, you write (in any language):

> *I want a tool that lists all walls on the active level with their thickness in millimeters.*

Claude:
1. Checks whether a similar tool already exists
2. Generates pyRevit handler code + MCP manifest
3. Validates the code via pyRevit
4. Installs it in your personal library
5. Tests it immediately on the open Revit project
6. Shows you the result

20-40 seconds from prompt to working, persistent, reusable tool — shareable with colleagues.

### Examples of tools you can generate

- *"Count the elements in my current selection and tell me their categories"*
- *"List the doors on the active level with their dimensions"*
- *"On the selected walls, set the comment to the text I pass"*
- *"Delete walls below a given height — show me a preview first"*

---

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────┐     MCP      ┌──────────────────────┐     HTTP     ┌────────────────────┐
│  Claude (Code/Desktop)│ ◀─stdio─▶ │  revit-mcp-server    │ ◀──REST───▶ │  Revit + pyRevit   │
│  + skill              │            │  (local Python)      │              │  (Routes server)   │
└──────────────────────┘             └──────────────────────┘              └────────────────────┘
        ↓                                       ↑
   "I want a tool that..."             ~/.revit-mcp/tools/
                                        (global library)
```

**Three components**, each with a single responsibility:

1. **pyRevit extension `RevitMcpRoutes`** — exposes HTTP routes inside Revit for managing the tool library
2. **`revit-mcp-server`** (Python) — MCP server that proxies between Claude and pyRevit
3. **Skill `revit-mcp-tool-generator`** — markdown content that teaches Claude how to generate safe, working tools

Generated tools are `(manifest.json, handler.py)` pairs saved both in `~/.revit-mcp/tools/` (user library) and in `RevitMcpRoutes.extension/lib/revit_mcp_routes/tools/`.

---

## Install

Five minutes on Windows.

### Prerequisites

- **Windows 10/11** with PowerShell 5+
- **Revit 2024** ⚠️ (the only tested version; other versions may work but are not officially supported)
- **pyRevit** 4.8+ ([download](https://github.com/pyrevitlabs/pyRevit/releases))
- **Python** 3.11+ ([download](https://www.python.org/downloads/))
- **Claude Code** (CLI) **or** Claude Desktop App ([download](https://claude.ai/download))

### Quick install

1. Download the latest release from the [Releases page](https://github.com/studioliquid-lab/revit-mcp-tool-generator/releases) (a single `.zip`)
2. Extract to a stable folder (e.g. `C:\Tools\revit-mcp-tool-generator\`)
3. **Double-click `setup.bat`**
4. Restart Revit + Claude
5. In Claude write: *"Use the sample_read tool and tell me how many walls you find"* → verify it works

Detailed instructions: see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) (Italian) — English translation coming soon.

---

## Sharing tools with the community

Each tool is two files. To package it:

```powershell
.\export-tool.ps1 -Name list_walls_by_level
```

Output: `list_walls_by_level.tool.zip` (~1-2 KB), shareable via email/cloud. A colleague imports it with:

```powershell
.\import-tool.ps1 -Zip "list_walls_by_level.tool.zip"
```

The import script validates the tool on the destination machine before installing.

---

## Known limitations

- **Windows only**: Revit only runs on Windows
- **Hot-reload of new tools in Claude Desktop App**: client-side limitation (Code CLI works perfectly, Desktop App requires restart after each new tool)
- **Single Revit version per install**: to change Revit version, edit `~/.revit-mcp/config.toml` or re-run `setup.bat`
- **Python 3.11+** required for the MCP server (pyRevit uses IronPython 2.7 but is handled automatically)

- **Pull requests** adding patterns to the cookbook

## Roadmap

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release history and intent.

Areas of future exploration (ordered by likelihood):

- **v0.2**: local LLM wiki of Revit docs (replaces on-demand WebFetch, works offline)
- **v0.3**: simultaneous multi-version Revit
- **v0.4**: composite tools (macros that call other tools)
- **v1.0**: API stabilization + community tool marketplace
